{{nihongo|'''Nireyama Shrine'''|楡山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Nireyama Shrine''' (にれやまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Haragō, {{ill|Fukaya, Saitama|Q734532|qid=Q734532}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}.

=== Overview ===
It is located northeast of JR {{ill|Fukaya Station|fr|Gare de Fukaya|id|Stasiun Fukaya|it|Stazione di Fukaya|ja|深谷駅|ko|후카야역|my|ဖုခယဘူတာ|simple|Fukaya Station|ur|فکایا اسٹیشن|zh|深谷站|qid=Q844895}} and Fukaya City Hall, on the south side of Gongendō Bridge on {{ill|Saitama Prefectural Road Route 127|ja|埼玉県道127号深谷飯塚線|qid=Q11426833|lt=Prefectural Route 127}}, which crosses the {{ill|Fuku River|ja|福川 (埼玉県)|qid=Q21654416|lt=Fukukawa River}}<ref name="kotobank">[https://kotobank.jp/word/楡山神社-3038796 楡山神社とは] - {{ill|Kotobank|ca|Kotobank|es|Kotobank|fa|کوتوبانک|fr|Kotobank|id|Kotobank|it|Kotobank|ja|コトバンク|ko|코토뱅크|pt|Kotobank|zh|Kotobank|zh_yue|Kotobank|qid=Q11302260}}</ref>.

Its foundation is traditionally said to date to the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōshō|Q312841|qid=Q312841}}<ref name="yuisho">[http://nireyama.main.jp/nire/ 由緒] - Nireyama Shrine</ref><ref name="jinjacho">[http://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/9944 楡山神社] - Saitama Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines</ref>. The surrounding area contains the {{ill|Kinomoto Kofun Cluster|ja|木の本古墳群|qid=Q17211800}}, and Nireyama Shrine is identified with the same-named {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Musashi Province|ja|武蔵国の式内社一覧|qid=Q11546334|lt=Shikinaisha}}; in any case, its history is very old and its origin is thought to go back to ancient times<ref name="kotobank"/><ref name="yuisho"/><ref name="jinjacho"/>.

The shrine name is said to come from the many {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=elm}} trees (nire) in the sacred precinct<ref name="yuisho"/><ref name="jinjacho"/>.

In the Edo period, the Tendai temple Tōgakuin became its {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}, and the shrine came to be called "Kumano Sansha Daigongen" and "Kumano-sha," but local people continued to call it Nireyama Shrine, as recorded in the ''{{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qid=Q11503943}}''<ref name="kotobank"/>.
